title: podman cp fails for image-mount subpaths on created containers
body:
@Honny1 reported this while reviewing #29842 ([original comment](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29842#pullrequestreview-5352696472)).

With `type=image,subpath=/bin`, copying `/mnt/ls` from a created container fails with `ENOENT`. The same copy succeeds after the container starts.

Reproducer from the review:

```bash
ctr="img-cp-test"
./bin/podman rm -f "$ctr" 2>/dev/null

./bin/podman create --name "$ctr" --network=none --mount "type=image,source=alpine,dst=/mnt,subpath=/bin" alpine sleep 3600
./bin/podman cp "$ctr:/mnt/ls" /tmp/from-created
# Error: no such file or directory

./bin/podman start "$ctr"
./bin/podman cp "$ctr:/mnt/ls" /tmp/from-running
# succeeds

./bin/podman exec "$ctr" ls -l /mnt/ls
./bin/podman rm -f "$ctr"
```

Expected: `podman cp` should find `/mnt/ls` in the created container too.

This is separate from #29840, which covers named-volume subpaths. The review used `./bin/podman`; full `podman info` was not provided.
